sections.h2: Where an Isabella County deed gets filed
sections.html:
Filing happens in Room 220 of the county building at 200 N. Main Street, Mount Pleasant, MI 48858. The office phone is (989) 317-4089. Land records here reach back to the mid-1800s, and a recorded document is open for anyone to review or copy. Staff neither draft documents nor answer legal questions, so a lawyer or closing company should finish the paperwork first.

Mount Pleasant is the county seat. When your house sells, the closing deed lands at this counter, and the office urges a careful read against the recording rules before anything is handed in.

State law sets a flat $30.00 for each document. If a document lists several liber and page references, each one beyond the first costs $3.00. Mail-in filers who want the original back should send a prepaid return envelope.

Isabella County recording and certification charges
ServiceCharge
Recording, per document$30.00 flat
Each additional liber and page listed$3.00 (first one free)
Tax certificate, up to 5 descriptions$5.00
Tax certificate, each description past 5$0.20
Name search by the office$0.50 per year searched, $5.00 minimum

Tax certificate checks are payable to the Isabella County Treasurer. Copies from a search carry the statutory copy fee, which the office will quote.

sections.h2: Which sales need a tax certificate first?
sections.html:
Section 211.135 of Michigan law requires a treasurer certificate before the office will file any of these:

  • Warranty deeds, plus any other deed with a covenant of warranty written into it.
  • Land contracts, and their assignments when a warranty clause is attached.
  • Condominium master deeds.

The treasurer issues it, so the check goes to the Isabella County Treasurer. Parcels with many descriptions pay 20 cents for each one after the fifth. Have your closing agent request the certificate before signing day so it cannot delay the filing.

The county posts a summary of the Michigan recording rules people ask about most, and refers readers to the legislature's website for the full text. Highlights from that list:

  • Original signatures only, each name typed, stamped or printed below, and no mismatch among the body text, the signature and the acknowledgment.
  • Every party's address is shown on any instrument that conveys, assigns or encumbers title.
  • A deed signed in the state is acknowledged by a notary and names its drafter with an address.
  • If the grantor section names a survivor, a certified death certificate is filed as a separate document.
  • A trust agreement attached to an instrument is filed on its own under Public Act 194 of 2018.
  • Court orders arrive certified and sealed by the clerk of the court.
  • Page one leaves 2 1/2 inches blank at the top, other margins run 1/2 inch, and the type is black, 10 point or larger, on white paper.
  • Any part written in another language needs an English translation attached.

Public Acts 191 through 200 of 2018 changed some of these rules, and the legislature's site has the details.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on an Isabella County sale
sections.html:
Two Michigan laws tax real estate transfers: Act 330 of 1993 at the state level and Act 134 of 1966 for counties. The dollar amount at your sale price comes from the Register of Deeds, and the settlement statement will show it.

A few statutory exemptions come up with house transfers, and the deed must carry the claim:

  • Spouses moving property into or out of entireties ownership.
  • Boundary-line adjustments made without payment.
  • Corrective quitclaims that only confirm a title the grantee already holds.
  • New joint tenancies where one of the co-owners already had the property.

Gifts to a child or grandchild are exempt only in the state act, so a family gift needs a question to the office first.

sections.h2: What to gather before the deed goes in
sections.html:
A complete package avoids a second trip to Mount Pleasant. Pull these items together with your closing agent:

  • The signed, notarized original deed, with the drafter's name and address on it.
  • A check for $30.00 to cover the recording, plus $3.00 for each extra liber and page.
  • The treasurer's tax certificate and its separate check, when the deed has warranty language.
  • The transfer tax payment or a stated exemption.
  • A return envelope, stamped and addressed, if the package goes by mail.

Once the office records the deed, it becomes a public record, and any buyer, lender or neighbor can pull a copy. That is why a clean filing matters.

The paperwork is the same, yet the buyer pool differs. Central Michigan University sits in the county, and 61.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied, with renters in 39.9 percent of occupied units at the 2020 census. For a landlord selling a rental near campus, that means a deed from an investor-owned property that may have tenants in place. Read any lease before you fix a closing date.

Part of Mount Pleasant also lies within the Isabella Indian Reservation, which spans 217.67 square miles and is the main land base of the Saginaw Chippewa Tribal Nation. Your title company can tell you whether your parcel sits inside the reservation and whether that changes the paperwork.

If the Treasurer shows unpaid tax on your parcel, the certificate for a warranty deed cannot be issued cleanly until it is dealt with. Call the Treasurer for the amount, hand it to your closing agent, and it comes out of your proceeds at closing. A sale to a cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal but not this step. If you plan to mail the package, send it early with a prepaid return envelope, since the office cannot return the recorded deed without one. After recording, ask your closing agent for a copy of the recorded deed and keep it with your sale papers, because the county's index is the public proof that ownership moved to the buyer.
Isabella County had 64,691 residents in mid-2025. A typical owned home is valued at $170,400, and median rent is $913 a month.

sections.h2: How the next tax bill changes after a sale
sections.html:
Selling resets taxable value: under Proposal A the cap lifts in the calendar year following the transfer. Form 2766, the Property Transfer Affidavit, is the paper the new owner sends to the local assessor. Some transfers are carved out of uncapping in subsection (7) of MCL 211.27a.

In Michigan, assessing is largely handled by cities and townships. The local assessor can tell you your taxable value and when the affidavit is due.

faqs.q: How much does a deed cost to file in Isabella County?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars flat per document, with $3.00 added for every extra liber and page reference past the first. When a tax certificate is required, it runs $5.00 for up to five descriptions.

faqs.q: Who issues the tax certificate for an Isabella County warranty deed?
faqs.a: The county treasurer's office. Your check for the certificate is payable to the Treasurer, and it must be obtained before the Register of Deeds records a warranty deed, land contract or condominium master deed.

faqs.q: How do I get my filed deed returned by mail?
faqs.a: Include a self-addressed, stamped return envelope with the package. Without it the office has no way to mail the recorded paper back.

faqs.q: Will Isabella County staff review my deed for legal problems?
faqs.a: No. The office neither drafts papers nor answers legal questions. An attorney handles that, and you should check the recording requirements before you submit.

faqs.q: What does a name search cost at the Isabella County office?
faqs.a: Fifty cents for every year searched, set by MCL 600.2567, with a $5.00 floor. Copies pulled from a search are billed at the statutory copy rate.
